summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) worked in indology and history and archaeology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and University of the Punjab/Panjab University. She held posts at Marg Publications, College of Art, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Kay Koppedrayer is a scholar in religious studies and indology who earned a BA from McGill University and an MA from McMaster University. She is retired from Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2005).

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster at Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and lecturer at the University of Calcutta (1920).

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He served as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1956–1965) and as professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1965–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees at Waseda University. He held posts at Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University, where he served from 1995 to 2013.

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He taught at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1982–1990) and later became professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Nagoya University (BA), Hokkaido University (master's), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc). He served as a professor of geography at Kyoto University from around 2012 to 2024.

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1948 to 1954. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–1998).

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, and Cornell universities under Teizo Iyanaga and Jay Jasanoff, and held posts at Nagoya City Women's College and Nagoya City University.
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Bukkyo University, attested in 2001 and 2013.

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University, where he later served as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazumi Yoshizaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1955) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto. He was a lecturer at Otani University and later served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, and served as an assistant professor at Otani University from ~1983 to 2014.

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his MA at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, later holding posts at Koyasan and Komazawa universities.

Kazuo Matsumura (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1973–1977) and later held positions at Tenri University (~1986–1992) and Wako University (~2004).

Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, and served as an associate professor (1973) and professor (1979–2006) at Komazawa University.

Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts as assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
